thread:
liz_sales: Quick one during POC handoff - customer has a dual-region TGW setup and wants PrivateLink into our connector in us-east-1 with failover to an outbound egress proxy in us-west-2. They also require source IP preservation for downstream auth logs and need to know firewall port list and cost deltas vs Hosted. Any known limitations?

omar_se: Summary: Use a regional interface endpoint in us-east-1 backed by a cross-account NLB in our service VPC. For cross-region fallback, use a regional proxy endpoint in us-west-2 and control routing via BGP local-preference on their edge or AWS route table automation. Keep in mind PrivateLink endpoints are regional and you can't attach a single endpoint across regions.

kevin_netops: Important: source IP preserved if you use a TCP NLB with instance targets and avoid SNAT. If traffic transits a NAT gateway or a proxy that SNATs, you lose source IP. For ingress from their TGW spoke, the source will show as the endpoint ENI unless they use IP prefixes; ensure SGs/ACLs accept the endpoint ENIs or their spoke CIDRs as necessary.

liz_sales: Rita, can you confirm whether your SDS-WAN->TGW supports BGP? We need either BGP path-preference or an external health-check automation to flip routes for region failover.

rita_customer: We have BGP across our SD-WAN into the TGW. We can set local-pref. We also prefer not to terminate TLS at the edge (no TLS inspect), so we should keep TLS end-to-end.

omar_se: Good. With TLS end-to-end, mutual TLS is an option for authenticating connections while preserving original IPs. Health-based failover approaches: 1) BGP local-pref change on fail; 2) TGW route table automation to switch prefix list target; 3) Client-side retry with latency-based DNS (not ideal for strict source IP requirements). We'll draft a minimal automation runbook.

kevin_netops: Firewall checklist (minimal):
- Allow outbound TCP 443 from spoke/TGW to our endpoint IPs (endpoint ENIs appear in their VPC)
- Allow inbound from our NLB health check ranges (we'll provide) to connector health port (e.g., 8080)
- If using client mTLS, allow TCP 443 and trust the client cert CNs we provide
- If they use an egress proxy in us-west-2 for failover, allow spoke->proxy TCP 443 and proxy->us-east NLB TCP 443 for control-plane probes

omar_se: Cost notes: PrivateLink (interface endpoint) = hourly ENI + per-GB processing. NLB = hourly + per-GB. Hosted API: no PrivateLink setup, simple HTTPS over public internet, variable per-token cost with no infra setup. Dedicated: reserved infra lowers per-token but needs monthly commit and can host the proxy in-region to reduce cross-region egress. We'll give a rough 1TB/month sketch.

infra-bot: Created ticket POC-8892: "regional-privatelink-failover-proxy" assigned to kevin_netops,omar_se - https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/POC-8892

liz_sales: Action items: kevin draft runbook for BGP local-pref flip + AWS route automation; omar to estimate endpoint+NLB+cross-region egress costs for 1TB baseline; I'll send a handoff diagram and ask about certificate exchange for mTLS.

rita_customer: Thanks - please include any MTU/overlay recommendations. We've seen issues before with SD-WAN overlays.

kevin_netops: Quick MTU note: SD-WAN overlays reduce effective MTU; recommend MSS clamp at their edge and test with large payload streaming. We'll include iptables example and a note about TCP window scaling oddities.

liz_sales: Great, please drop runbook & cost sketch in the ticket by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:

rita_customer: Appreciated, looking forward to the diagram and runbook.
